"'''Unbelievable'''" is a song written and performed by British band [[EMF (band)|EMF]], originally appearing on their debut album, ''[[Schubert Dip]]'' (1991). It was released as a single in the UK in October 1990 by [[Parlophone]], peaking at number three on the [[UK Singles Chart]] on 1 December 1990. It was the 30th-best-selling single of 1990 in the UK,<ref>{{cite web |title=Official Top 40 best-selling songs of 1990 |url=https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/official-top-40-best-selling-songs-of-1990__33128/ |website=Official Charts.com |access-date=13 February 2024}}</ref> and a top-10 hit also in Belgium, Germany, Ireland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Spain and Sweden. In the United States, "Unbelievable" hit number one on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] and [[Cash Box Top 100 Pop Singles|''Cash Box'' Top 100]] in 1991. The song was produced by [[Ralph Jezzard]], and contains samples of US comedian [[Andrew Dice Clay]]<ref>{{cite book|first= Nick |last= Talevski |year= 2006 |title= Rock Obituaries – Knocking on Heaven's Door |publisher= [[Omnibus Press]] |page= 179 |isbn= 978-1-8460-9091-2 |url= https://books.google.com/books?id=DykffzkFALoC&pg=PA179}}</ref> and performance poet [[Gylan Kain]]. Its accompanying music video was directed by [[Josh Taft]], depicting the band performing onstage.

"Unbelievable" is a song written and performed by British band EMF, originally appearing on their debut album, Schubert Dip (1991). It was released as a single in the UK in October 1990 by Parlophone, peaking at number three on the UK Singles Chart on 1 December 1990. It was the 30th-best-selling single of 1990 in the UK, and a top-10 hit also in Belgium, Germany, Ireland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Spain and Sweden. In the United States, "Unbelievable" hit number one on the Billboard Hot 100 and Cash Box Top 100 in 1991. The song was produced by Ralph Jezzard, and contains samples of US comedian Andrew Dice Clay and performance poet Gylan Kain. Its accompanying music video was directed by Josh Taft, depicting the band performing onstage.

sections.heading: Background and release
Critical reception
sections.wikitext:
In 2018, Bill Lamb from [[About.com]] noted that the song "mixed intoxicating rhythms, sweet high vocals from lead singer James Atkin, and rousing shouts to storm to the top of the pop charts."<ref>{{cite web|first= Bill |last= Lamb |title= The Best 100 Songs from the 1990s |publisher= [[Dotdash|ThoughtCo]] |date= 23 September 2018 |url= https://www.thoughtco.com/top-songs-from-the-90s-3245307 |archive-date= 7 May 2019 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20190507170253/https://www.thoughtco.com/top-songs-from-the-90s-3245307}}</ref> In his review of ''[[Schubert Dip]]'', [[AllMusic]] editor Alex Henderson described the song as "so insanely infectious",<ref>{{cite web|first= Alex |last= Henderson |title= EMF – Schubert Dip |publisher= [[AllMusic]] |access-date= 18 February 2020 |url= https://www.allmusic.com/album/schubert-dip-mw0000267414}}</ref> remarking its "dizzying infectiousness". Upon the release, [[J.D. Considine]] from ''[[The Baltimore Sun]]'' felt the group's material appeals as much to the brain as the body, so that songs such as "Unbelievable" "end up danceable, hummable, and utterly irresistible."<ref>[[J.D. Considine|Considine, J.D.]] (1991). "EMF – ''Schubert Dip''". ''[[Baltimore Sun]]'' – via ''[[Milwaukee Journal]]''. (9 June 1991).</ref> [[Larry Flick]] from ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' magazine declared it as an "insinuating, [[Madchester|Manchester]]-influenced rave. Scratchy, neopsychedelic guitar riffs nicely contrast track's [[hip hop music|hip hop]] groove, promising extensive exposure here at both club and radio levels."<ref>{{cite magazine|first= Larry |last= Flick |author-link= Larry Flick |title= Single Reviews > New and Noteworthy |magazine= [[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |date= 9 March 1991 |page= 79 |url= https://www.worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Billboard/90s/1991/BB-1991-03-09.pdf}}</ref> 

John Earls of ''[[Classic Pop (magazine)|Classic Pop]]'' called it "mighty".<ref>{{cite magazine|first= John |last= Earls |title= Boxset review – EMF 30th Anniversary Boxset |magazine= [[Classic Pop (magazine)|Classic Pop]] |date= March 2021 |accessdate= 31 August 2021 |url= https://www.classicpopmag.com/2021/03/boxset-review-emf-30th-anniversary-boxset/}}</ref> Annette Petruso from ''[[The Michigan Daily]]'' stated that the boys from the [[Forest of Dean]] "have created an undeniably perfect pop single with the ultra-simple, ultra-catchy and ultra-overplayed "Unbelievable"."<ref>{{cite news|first= Annette |last= Petruso |title= Sexy EMF needs a little bit o' respect |newspaper= [[The Michigan Daily]] |page= 5 |date= 13 November 1991 |access-date= 15 March 2020 |url= https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=Zv1JAAAAIBAJ&pg=3027%2C3374132}}</ref> [[Andrew Collins (broadcaster)|Andrew Collins]] from ''[[New Musical Express|NME]]'' complimented it as a "special record", writing, "It's their first, and it's crunchier than the breakfast cereal [[Start (cereal)|Start]]. Sex-flavoured bass, hoppity drums, unfettered guitar, and a shouting sample that might be stupid old [[Andrew Dice Clay]] for all I know — yes, it's got the lot. Drenched in all the same juices that make [[Pop Will Eat Itself|PWEI]] so cool, it even sounds like five people were involved in its construction. I believe."<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Andrew|last=Collins|magazine=[[New Musical Express|NME]]|title=Singles|url=https://www.flickr.com/photos/nothingelseon/52227694967/|date=27 October 1990|access-date=24 February 2023|author-link=Andrew Collins (broadcaster)}}</ref>
sections.text:
In 2018, Bill Lamb from About.com noted that the song "mixed intoxicating rhythms, sweet high vocals from lead singer James Atkin, and rousing shouts to storm to the top of the pop charts." In his review of Schubert Dip, AllMusic editor Alex Henderson described the song as "so insanely infectious", remarking its "dizzying infectiousness". Upon the release, J.D. Considine from The Baltimore Sun felt the group's material appeals as much to the brain as the body, so that songs such as "Unbelievable" "end up danceable, hummable, and utterly irresistible." Larry Flick from Billboard magazine declared it as an "insinuating, Manchester-influenced rave. Scratchy, neopsychedelic guitar riffs nicely contrast track's hip hop groove, promising extensive exposure here at both club and radio levels." 

John Earls of Classic Pop called it "mighty". Annette Petruso from The Michigan Daily stated that the boys from the Forest of Dean "have created an undeniably perfect pop single with the ultra-simple, ultra-catchy and ultra-overplayed "Unbelievable"." Andrew Collins from NME complimented it as a "special record", writing, "It's their first, and it's crunchier than the breakfast cereal Start. Sex-flavoured bass, hoppity drums, unfettered guitar, and a shouting sample that might be stupid old Andrew Dice Clay for all I know — yes, it's got the lot. Drenched in all the same juices that make PWEI so cool, it even sounds like five people were involved in its construction. I believe."

sections.heading: Chart performance
sections.wikitext: "Unbelievable" entered the top 10 in Belgium, Germany, Ireland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. In the UK, it peaked at number three on the [[UK Singles Chart]] during its fifth week, spending two weeks at that position. The single was also a top-10 hit on the [[Eurochart Hot 100]], peaking at number eight in December 1990.<ref name="eurocharthot100"/> Outside Europe, "Unbelievable" was a top-20 hit in New Zealand while entering the top 10 in Australia. In the United States, the song appeared on four different ''Billboard'' charts, peaking at number one on the [[Hot 100]], number nine on the [[Dance Club Songs|Dance Club Play]] chart, number five on the [[Dance Singles Sales|12-inch Singles Sales]] chart and number three on the [[Modern Rock Tracks]] chart. It also reached number one on the [[Cash Box Top 100 Pop Singles|''Cash Box'' Top 100]]. In Canada, "Unbelievable" reached number four on the ''[[RPM (magazine)|RPM]]'' 100 Hit Tracks chart and number three on the ''RPM'' Dance chart. In West Asia, it became a top-20 hit in Israel, peaking at number 14 on 23 December 1990.<ref name="israel">{{cite web|url=https://israelcharts.com/|title=Israeli Charts|date=23 December 1990|access-date=19 August 2026|archive-date=26 June 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260626205604/https://israelcharts.com/|url-status=live}} Search "Unbelievable" for Israeli chart history.</ref> The single earned a gold record in Australia, Canada and the US, as well as a silver record in the UK.
sections.text: "Unbelievable" entered the top 10 in Belgium, Germany, Ireland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. In the UK, it peaked at number three on the UK Singles Chart during its fifth week, spending two weeks at that position. The single was also a top-10 hit on the Eurochart Hot 100, peaking at number eight in December 1990. Outside Europe, "Unbelievable" was a top-20 hit in New Zealand while entering the top 10 in Australia. In the United States, the song appeared on four different Billboard charts, peaking at number one on the Hot 100, number nine on the Dance Club Play chart, number five on the 12-inch Singles Sales chart and number three on the Modern Rock Tracks chart. It also reached number one on the Cash Box Top 100. In Canada, "Unbelievable" reached number four on the RPM 100 Hit Tracks chart and number three on the RPM Dance chart. In West Asia, it became a top-20 hit in Israel, peaking at number 14 on 23 December 1990. The single earned a gold record in Australia, Canada and the US, as well as a silver record in the UK.

sections.text:
"Unbelievable" was awarded one of BMI's Pop Awards in 1992, honoring the songwriters, composers and music publishers of the song. The song was ranked No. 31 on VH1's "100 Greatest One-Hit Wonders" in 2002 and No. 98 on VH1's "100 Greatest Songs of the 90s" in 2007. In 2003, English music journalist Paul Morley included it in his list of "Greatest Pop Single of All Time". In 2011, Australian music channel Max included it in their list of "1000 Greatest Songs of All Time". In July 2014, Rolling Stone magazine listed "Unbelievable" at number 12 in their "20 Biggest Songs of the Summer: The 1990s" list. In 2020, Cleveland.com listed it at number 41 in their ranking of the best Billboard Hot 100 No. 1 song of the 1990s. In 2024, Billboard magazine ranked it number 52 in their "The 100 Greatest Jock Jams of All Time", naming it "Andrew Dice Clay’s greatest contribution to polite society."

A cover of the song with rewritten lyrics sung by Keely Hawkes was featured in the 2009 straight-to-DVD film Barbie and the Three Musketeers.

sections.heading: In popular culture
sections.wikitext:
From 2005 until 2006, a commercial for ''Kraft Natural Cheese Crumbles'' rewrote the chorus as "They're Crumbelievable!"<ref>{{cite web|title=Un-Crumbelievable|access-date=19 February 2006|via=IndieWire|url=https://indiewire.com/news/general/un-crumbelievable-2231111/}}</ref><ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KaXOGLpPAfU Crumbelievable!]</ref>.

In 2009, the song was used in a campaign title "Unbelievable Song"<ref>[https://adsspot.me/media/tv-commercial/coca-cola-zero-unbelievable-song-21aad88ba678 Coca-Cola Film Unbelievable Song by Wieden + Kennedy]</ref>(by Wieden + Kennedy) for the soda ''Coca-Cola Zero''.

In 2024, the song was used in a TV spot for the restaurant ''[[Applebee's]]'' to promote their low-price menu items such as $0.50 mozzarella sticks<ref>[https://www.ispot.tv/ad/6vRw/applebees-050-mozzarella-sticks-unbelievable-song-by-emf Applebee's $0.50 Mozzarella Sticks TV Spot, 'Unbelievable' Song by EMF]</ref> and their Irresist-A-Bowls<ref>[https://www.ispot.tv/ad/On_3/applebees-irresist-a-bowls-its-back-song-by-emf Applebee's Irresist-A-Bowls TV Spot, 'It's Back' Song by EMF]</ref>.

In 2026, a sample of the song can be heard in a commercial for ''ICOTYDE''<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YBNn2GbfxSo Icotyde Commercial (2026)]</ref>where it features a doctor reciting lines while a unicorn casually passes a window.
